movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Restricted or stylized; minimal movement in Irish stepdance, more expressive in stepping
movement_profile.difficulty: Beginner to advanced depending on complexity of footwork and speed
movement_profile.footwork: Intricate heel, toe, and sole strikes producing rhythmic beats; feet often close to the floor in traditional forms
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Solo, line, or group formations; African-American stepping uses synchronized group formations
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Generally stable with minor movement to support footwork
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily low-level footwork; jumps not emphasized in traditional step dance
movement_profile.partnering: Typically solo or group; not partner-based
movement_profile.posture: Upright torso with limited upper body movement; focus on controlled foot strikes

signature_moves.description: Striking the heel sharply on the floor to produce a percussive sound.
signature_moves.name: Heel Tap

signature_moves.description: Light tapping of the toe on the floor in rhythm.
signature_moves.name: Toe Dig

signature_moves.description: Quick brushing of the foot forward and backward on the floor.
signature_moves.name: Shuffle

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Varies from moderate to fast; precise timing essential
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Excessive upper body movement in styles where arms are restricted Improper timing that disrupts synchronization with music Wearing inappropriate footwear that does not produce clear percussive sounds

music_profile.meter: Commonly 2/4, 4/4, or 6/8 depending on dance type
music_profile.musical_form: Strathspey, reel, jig, and other traditional folk forms
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Percussive foot strikes aligned with musical beats; call-and-response in stepping
music_profile.sound_description: A percussive soundscape created by hard-soled shoes striking the floor in rhythmic patterns, often accompanied by fiddle-driven melodies and call-and-response vocals.
music_profile.tempo_bpm: Varies by style; Irish stepdance often 90-120 bpm
music_profile.vocal_style: Sometimes includes call-and-response chants, especially in African-American stepping

basic_steps: Strike heel on floor with controlled timing
Alternate feet to produce continuous beats
Maintain upright posture with minimal arm movement
teaching.formation: Solo or group formations depending on variant; African-American stepping often in synchronized groups; Irish stepdance typically solo or in lines
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic heel and toe strikes, focusing on timing and rhythm; advanced dancers incorporate complex foot patterns and speed
teaching.rhythm: Varies by style; commonly aligned with strathspey, reel, jig, or percussive call-and-response patterns
